What lets a bicycle roll? Choose from wheel, gear or lever.
Wheels turn and roll along the ground.
What cuts paper? Choose from hammer, screwdriver or scissors.
Safety scissors cut paper. Cut away from your body.
What drives a nail into wood? Choose from scissors, hammer or screwdriver.
A hammer drives in nails. An adult helps with this.
What turns a screw? Choose from screwdriver, hammer or scissors.
A screwdriver turns screws in or out.
What does a magnet attract: iron, wood or paper? Choose from wood, paper or iron.
Magnets attract iron. Not every metal is magnetic.
What carries a path across a river? Choose from lamp, bridge or wheel.
A bridge connects the two banks.
What lights up a dark corner? Choose from lamp, battery or gear.
A lamp gives off light when switched on.
What supplies energy to a battery-powered torch? Choose from lamp, gear or battery.
A battery stores energy for the torch. Never open it.
What protects your head when cycling? Choose from flower, helmet or paper.
A correctly fitted and fastened helmet protects your head.
What has teeth and passes on a turning movement? Choose from gear, wheel or lever.
Gear teeth fit together to pass on turning movements.
Which device tilts around a pivot? Choose from battery, paper or lever.
A seesaw is a lever with a pivot.
What changes a rope's direction when lifting? Choose from gear, pulley or lever.
A rope runs over a pulley, so you can pull down to lift something.
Which material can you see through clearly? Choose from glass, wood or iron.
Clear glass lets lots of light through.
Which building material comes from trees? Choose from iron, glass or wood.
Wood comes from tree trunks and branches.
Which material makes a soft cloth? Choose from iron, fabric or glass.
Fabric bends easily and can be made into a cloth.
What can you draw a building plan on? Choose from paper, sand or oil.
You can draw a plan on paper before you build.
What helps you find north? Choose from hammer, scissors or compass.
A compass needle lines up roughly towards north.
What can push a ball that is still? Choose from moon, hand or cloud.
A hand can exert a force on the ball and make it move.
What forms when ice is melting? Choose from water, oil or water vapour.
Melting changes solid ice into liquid water.
What casts a clear shadow in lamp light: wood, clear glass or clear water? Choose from glass, water or wood.
A wooden block blocks the light and casts a clear shadow.
What usually floats: a light dry piece of wood, an iron block or sand? Choose from sand, wood or iron.
Many light woods float in water. A solid iron block sinks.
Which material lets light pass through clearly? Choose from glass, iron or wood.
Clear glass is transparent. Iron blocks and wood blocks are not.
Which body part detects sound waves? Choose from nose, eye or ear.
Your ears detect vibrations travelling through the air as sound.
What best softens tapping sounds on a table: a soft cloth, glass or iron? Choose from iron, fabric or glass.
A soft cloth can damp vibrations and tapping sounds.
Which makes its own light: the sun, the moon or a cloud? Choose from sun, moon or cloud.
The sun gives off its own light. The moon and clouds reflect light.
Which of these has its own solid shape? Choose from oil, water or ice.
An ice cube is solid. Liquids such as water and oil take the shape of their container.
What forms invisibly when water evaporates? Choose from water, water vapour or ice.
Invisible water vapour forms. The white cloud in the game is only a symbol.
What gives off light and warmth that can melt ice outdoors? Choose from sun, moon or cloud.
The sun supplies energy. Ice melts when it warms enough.
What shows roads and paths in a drawing? Choose from globe, compass or map.
A map shows paths from above on a smaller scale.
How do you hear a bicycle bell? Choose from nose, ear or eye.
Your ears detect the sound of the bell.
Which material is normally used for a strong bicycle wheel axle? Choose from iron, glass or wood.
A metal axle can support and guide a wheel.
Which structure needs strong supports? Choose from soap, egg or bridge.
A bridge needs a strong structure and suitable supports.
What soaks up water well when drying: fabric, glass or iron? Choose from iron, fabric or glass.
An absorbent cloth holds water between its fibres.
What supplies energy to a solar cell? Choose from sun, moon or egg.
A solar cell turns sunlight into electrical energy.
What turns on a moving bicycle? Choose from scissors, salt or wheel.
The wheels turn as the bicycle moves forward.
What is a transparent window pane made of? Choose from wood, glass or fabric.
Clear glass lets plenty of light into a room.
Which material can fabric scissors cut? Choose from fabric, glass or iron.
Fabric scissors cut fabric. They do not cut glass or an iron block.
Which part of a pulley turns? Choose from leaf, salt or wheel.
The pulley's round wheel turns as the rope moves.
What goes in a toy lamp's battery compartment? Choose from gear, battery or lamp.
Only the correct batteries go there. An adult helps replace them.
What has a north pole and a south pole? Choose from magnet, roots or cloud.
A magnet has two poles. Matching poles repel each other.
Where can a fish breathe with gills? Choose from water, sand or cloud.
Fish use gills to take oxygen from water.
Where does a blackbird hatch its eggs? Choose from glass, oil or nest.
Blackbirds build nests for their eggs and chicks.
Where does a bee find nectar? Choose from roots, flower or seed.
Many flowers contain nectar that bees collect.
What takes water from the soil into a tree? Choose from roots, leaf or flower.
Roots take water from the soil.
What does a seed need to start growing? Choose from oil, salt or water.
Many seeds need water, air and suitable warmth to germinate.
What gives a green plant light to grow? Choose from iron, sun or moon.
Green plants use sunlight to make food.
Which animal develops from a caterpillar? Choose from butterfly, frog or fish.
A caterpillar becomes a pupa. A butterfly emerges from it.
Which animal grows from a tadpole? Choose from bird, cat or frog.
A frog tadpole develops into a frog with legs.
What can hatch from a hen's egg? Choose from fish, bird or frog.
A chick can hatch from a fertilised hen's egg that is kept warm.
Which animal is a mammal? Choose from cat, turtle or butterfly.
Mother cats feed their kittens with milk.
Which animal has feathers? Choose from earthworm, fish or bird.
Birds have feathers, which help keep them warm.
Which animal has a hard shell? Choose from mouse, turtle or bee.
A turtle has a shell that is part of its body.
Which animal loosens soil as it burrows? Choose from earthworm, bird or cat.
Earthworms make tunnels in the soil.
What can grow into a new apple tree? Choose from leaf, flower or seed.
An apple contains seeds that can grow into new trees.
Which animal can pollinate flowers? Choose from turtle, bee or fish.
Bees carry pollen from one flower to another.
Which green plant parts form the tree crown here? Choose from leaf, roots or seed.
Many trees have leaves that absorb light.
Which is a fungus rather than a plant? Choose from flower, bird or mushroom.
Fungi form their own group. Never eat an unknown mushroom.
What does a cat need to drink every day? Choose from salt, water or oil.
Cats need fresh drinking water.
What might a blackbird eat? Choose from earthworm, fish or turtle.
Blackbirds eat earthworms and berries, among other foods.
Where can a butterfly drink nectar? Choose from seed, roots or flower.
Many butterflies use a long mouthpart to drink nectar from flowers.
Which of these animals lives in water? Choose from bee, fish or cat.
The fish in the picture lives in water.
Where does a common frog lay its eggs? Choose from water, leaf or sand.
Common frogs lay their eggs in water.
What grows into the soil first when a seed sprouts? Choose from flower, apple or roots.
A small root grows into the soil first.
What do roots absorb? Choose from sand, water or oil.
Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals.
Where do many trees grow close together? Choose from forest, sea or desert.
Many trees grow together in a forest.
Which parts of the tree crown often turn yellow or red in autumn? Choose from roots, seed or leaf.
Many broadleaf trees have leaves that turn yellow, red or brown in autumn.
Which animal has a beak? Choose from turtle, bird or cat.
Birds have beaks, often shaped to suit their food.
Which of these animals is an insect? Choose from bee, fish or earthworm.
A bee is an insect. Insects have six legs.
What do young turtles hatch from? Choose from apple, seed or egg.
Turtles lay eggs, and their young hatch from them.
What can form after flowering and grow into new plants? Choose from soap, seed or iron.
Seeds can form after pollination.
What does a cat use to hear? Choose from ear, eye or nose.
Cats hear with their ears.
Which is a living thing: a mouse, paper or glass? Choose from paper, glass or mouse.
A mouse is alive: it grows, breathes and needs food.
What should you leave undisturbed when watching bird eggs? Choose from soap, nest or wheel.
Watch a nest from a distance so the parents feel safe.
Which plant part holds a flower in the ground? Choose from roots, leaf or seed.
Roots anchor the plant in the soil.
A plant's soil is dry. What might it need? Choose from salt, oil or water.
The plant may need water. Give the amount that suits that plant.
What helps bees in a garden? Choose from hammer, flower or glass.
A variety of flowers provides food for bees.
What can earthworms pull into the soil? Choose from leaf, battery or glass.
Earthworms pull fallen, dead leaves into their burrows.
What do pond fish swim in? Choose from sand, oil or water.
A pond contains water and is home to different animals.
What can grow from an acorn? Choose from iron, tree or wheel.
An acorn is an oak seed. It can grow into a tree.
Which adult animal has four wings? Choose from butterfly, bird or cat.
A butterfly has two forewings and two hindwings.
What does ice become when it melts? Choose from water, sand or iron.
Ice is frozen water. Melting turns it into liquid water.
What can water become in a freezer? Choose from salt, paper or ice.
When water gets cold enough, it can freeze into ice.
Which is liquid at room temperature? Choose from glass, water or wood.
Water is liquid at normal room temperature.
Which is solid at room temperature? Choose from wood, oil or water.
A block of wood has a fixed shape.
Which container reliably holds drinking water? Choose from paper, fabric or glass.
An undamaged drinking glass does not let water pass through.
What dissolves in water: salt, sand or wood? Choose from wood, salt or sand.
Small amounts of salt dissolve in water. The salt is still there.
What stays visible as grains in water? Choose from sand, salt or water.
Sand does not normally dissolve in water.
What often forms two layers with water? Choose from salt, paper or oil.
Cooking oil and water do not stay mixed.
Which object attracts iron out of a mixture? Choose from scissors, magnet or lever.
A magnet attracts iron. The metal picture here stands for iron.
What forms invisibly when water evaporates? Choose from water vapour, ice or water.
Water becomes invisible water vapour. The white cloud is only a symbol for it.
What are the little drops on a cold window made of? Choose from water vapour, ice or water.
Water vapour in the air can turn into liquid water on cold glass.
Which form of water is solid? Choose from water vapour, ice or water.
Frozen water is called ice.
Which symbol stands for water as a gas? Choose from water vapour, water or ice.
Water as a gas is invisible. The vapour cloud is a simplified symbol.
What dissolves a little table salt well? Choose from oil, fabric or water.
A little salt dissolves in water. Never taste an unknown substance.
Which material is transparent? Choose from paper, glass or wood.
Clear glass lets light through so you can see through it.
Which material easily soaks up water? Choose from paper, iron or glass.
Uncoated paper absorbs water between its fibres.
What can be softly folded up? Choose from iron, glass or fabric.
A fabric cloth bends easily. A metal bar is much stiffer.
Which material can conduct heat well? Choose from paper, iron or fabric.
Many metals conduct heat well. Never touch hot objects.
Which material often shows growth rings? Choose from wood, glass or iron.
Wood comes from trees. Growth rings are often visible in a cut section.
What helps grease mix with water so it can be washed away? Choose from sand, oil or soap.
Soap helps water remove grease and dirt.
Which substance is often used in cooking and stays liquid? Choose from salt, oil or ice.
Many cooking oils are liquid at room temperature.
Which of these consists of many little grains? Choose from sand, glass or water.
Sand consists of many small solid grains.
What provides warmth that can melt ice outdoors? Choose from moon, snow or sun.
The sun supplies energy. Heat can make ice melt.
Where do many tiny water drops gather in the sky? Choose from moon, cloud or sun.
Clouds contain tiny water droplets or ice crystals.
What are raindrops mainly made of? Choose from water, oil or salt.
Raindrops are mainly liquid water.
What are snowflakes made of? Choose from sand, iron or ice.
Snowflakes are made of ice crystals.
What takes the shape of a glass? Choose from iron, water or paper.
Liquid water does not have its own fixed shape.
What keeps its own shape on a plate before warming up? Choose from ice, water or oil.
An ice cube is solid and keeps its shape until it melts.
Which material can shatter if dropped? Choose from fabric, paper or glass.
Glass can break. Let an adult clear away the pieces.
Which product is intended for washing hands with water? Choose from salt, soap or oil.
Soap is made for skin. Unknown cleaning products are not toys.
What is left when salt water completely evaporates? Choose from salt, sand or ice.
The water evaporates. Dissolved salt can remain as crystals.
Which object attracts iron pieces out of sand? Choose from scissors, hammer or magnet.
A magnet attracts the iron pieces, but normally not the sand.
Which substance flows from a tipped open bottle? Choose from glass, water or wood.
Liquid water flows and needs a watertight container.
What is often made from plant fibres? Choose from paper, glass or iron.
Paper contains connected fibres, often from wood.
What is the same substance as water, but solid? Choose from water vapour, oil or ice.
Ice and liquid water are the same substance in different states.
What is ordinary glass mainly made from? Choose from iron, sand or wood.
Silica sand is an important ingredient in glass, made in very hot furnaces.
Which material can be made from woven threads? Choose from fabric, glass or iron.
Many fabrics are woven from threads.
What rinses soap off your hands? Choose from oil, salt or water.
Clean water rinses away soap and loosened dirt.
What stays solid in water at room temperature: glass, ice or salt? Choose from salt, glass or ice.
A drinking glass does not dissolve in water during normal use.
What does an ice cube become when it melts in a glass? Choose from water, water vapour or oil.
Melting changes solid ice to liquid water. It does not make a new substance.
Which body part detects light and colours? Choose from eye, ear or nose.
Eyes detect light and send signals to the brain.
Which body part detects sounds? Choose from nose, eye or ear.
Ears detect sounds. The brain processes the signals.
What do people use to smell? Choose from tongue, nose or eye.
The nose contains cells that detect smells.
What helps you taste sweet and sour? Choose from tongue, nose or ear.
The tongue has many taste buds.
What can feel whether a cloth is soft? Choose from eye, ear or hand.
The skin on your hand contains touch receptors.
Which organ pumps blood around the body? Choose from stomach, heart or lungs.
The heart is a muscle that pumps blood through blood vessels.
Which organs take in air when you breathe? Choose from lungs, heart or stomach.
In the lungs, oxygen moves from the air into the blood.
Which organ processes information from your senses? Choose from heart, stomach or brain.
The brain processes signals and controls many activities.
What forms the body's hard framework? Choose from lungs, bone or heart.
The bones together form the skeleton.
What breaks food into smaller pieces in your mouth? Choose from tooth, tongue or ear.
Teeth break up food when you chew.
Where does food go after the food pipe? Choose from heart, lungs or stomach.
Food moves through the food pipe into the stomach.
What helps wash your hands clean? Choose from sand, soap or oil.
Wash with water and soap, including between your fingers.
What is a good drink when you are thirsty? Choose from water, salt or oil.
Clean drinking water quenches thirst without added sugar.
Which picture here stands for nighttime and bedtime? Choose from sun, cloud or moon.
Night is dark. Sleep gives the body time to rest.
Which body part often wears a shoe? Choose from eye, foot or hand.
Shoes protect feet. People move in different ways.
What protects your head when cycling? Choose from helmet, soap or paper.
A well-fitted helmet can protect your head if you fall.
Which sense needs protection from very loud sounds? Choose from eye, nose or ear.
Very loud sounds can harm hearing. Turn the volume down.
Which body part do eyelids protect? Choose from tongue, eye or nose.
Eyelids protect the eyes. Blinking spreads tear fluid.
Which body part helps filter the air you breathe in? Choose from nose, ear or tongue.
The nose filters, warms and moistens incoming air.
What do many children lose and replace as they grow? Choose from bone, hand or tooth.
Baby teeth gradually make way for adult teeth.
Which body part usually has five fingers? Choose from ear, hand or foot.
A hand usually has five fingers. Bodies can look different.
What usually beats faster when you exercise? Choose from heart, lungs or stomach.
The heart often beats faster to bring muscles more oxygen.
Where does air go when you breathe in? Choose from heart, stomach or lungs.
Air travels through the airways into the lungs.
Where are many memories processed? Choose from stomach, brain or heart.
The brain helps you learn and remember.
What protects the brain as the skull? Choose from bone, brain or heart.
The skull bones surround and protect the brain.
Which organ mixes food and continues digestion? Choose from heart, lungs or stomach.
The stomach churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
Which part of the body senses smells while you eat? Choose from ear, nose or tongue.
Smell and taste work together when you eat.
What do you use to wash your hands before eating? Choose from soap, oil or salt.
Water and soap help remove dirt and many germs.
Which of these is food? Choose from battery, soap or apple.
A washed apple is food. Batteries and soap are not.
What is inside a foot and gives it support? Choose from heart, bone or tooth.
A foot contains many bones that work together for support.
Which organ processes signals from your ears so you recognize sounds? Choose from brain, heart or stomach.
The signals go to the brain, which processes sounds.
Where do eyes send their signals? Choose from heart, stomach or brain.
Eyes send signals to the brain, where images are processed.
Which organ brings oxygen from air into the blood? Choose from stomach, lungs or heart.
Oxygen can enter the blood in the tiny air sacs of the lungs.
Which organ is a strong muscle in the chest? Choose from heart, lungs or stomach.
The heart is a muscle that works even while you sleep.
What usually feels soft and bendy? Choose from glass, iron or fabric.
You can feel and fold a soft cloth with your hand.
Which body part do you clean with a toothbrush? Choose from ear, tooth or nose.
Teeth need regular cleaning. An adult can help finish brushing.
What can you breathe through when resting? Choose from nose, eye or ear.
When resting, air can enter through your nose.
What helps you hear this game's music? Choose from eye, nose or ear.
The ears detect music. Keep it at a comfortable, quiet volume.
What does the body need to drink? Choose from salt, water or oil.
Drinking water provides the body with fluid.
What can gently hold a soft ball? Choose from hand, bone or tooth.
Hands and fingers can hold a ball. People also use helpful tools.
What shows Earth as a small sphere? Choose from globe, map or compass.
A globe is a small model of Earth.
Which drawing on a flat sheet shows places and paths from above? Choose from globe, compass or map.
A map shows part of the world from above on a smaller scale.
Which instrument has a needle that points north? Choose from globe, compass or map.
A compass helps you find north and the other directions.
What rises high above the land around it? Choose from mountain, river or sea.
A mountain is a high landform.
What flows in a channel through the landscape? Choose from desert, forest or river.
A river carries water along its riverbed.
What is land surrounded by water on all sides? Choose from cloud, island or mountain.
An island is surrounded by water on every side.
Where can you find a very large amount of salt water? Choose from sea, forest or desert.
Seas contain salt water and cover large parts of Earth.
Where is there very little precipitation over a long time? Choose from river, forest or desert.
Deserts get very little precipitation. Some deserts are cold.
Where do many trees grow together? Choose from sand, forest or sea.
A forest has many trees and is home to many animals.
What can fall from clouds to the ground? Choose from rain, sun or moon.
Rain falls from some clouds and brings water to the ground.
What falls from the sky as ice crystals? Choose from rain, cloud or snow.
Snow consists of ice crystals that fall from clouds.
What gives Earth light and warmth? Choose from cloud, sun or moon.
The sun supplies Earth with light and warmth.
What orbits Earth? Choose from moon, sun or cloud.
The moon moves around Earth.
What connects two banks so a path can cross? Choose from sand, cloud or bridge.
A bridge crosses an obstacle such as a river.
Where do many large rivers eventually flow? Choose from forest, sea or mountain.
Many rivers flow into the sea. Others end in lakes or inland.
What can remain as a frozen white layer on high mountains even in summer? Choose from snow, rain or cloud.
High up it is often colder, so snow can remain there.
What is often coloured blue on maps? Choose from forest, desert or water.
On many maps, blue stands for water such as rivers and seas.
What does a forest symbol on a map show? Choose from mountain, forest or sea.
A forest symbol shows where a forest is. The key explains the symbols.
What does a bridge symbol on a map show? Choose from bridge, river or mountain.
It shows a crossing over a river or another obstacle.
What covers most of Earth’s surface? Choose from forest, desert or sea.
Seas cover more than half of Earth's surface.
Where do raindrops form in the sky? Choose from wood, cloud or iron.
Tiny drops in clouds can join together and fall as rain.
What mainly warms water in Earth’s water cycle? Choose from sun, moon or cloud.
Warmth from the sun helps water evaporate.
How can water return from clouds to the ground? Choose from sand, wood or rain.
Precipitation such as rain returns water to the ground.
Where can a river begin high above the plains? Choose from fabric, mountain or sea.
Many rivers begin in mountains, but not all do.
What lies in little grains on many beaches? Choose from sand, water or wood.
Many beaches have sand. Others have pebbles or rocks.
What is especially scarce in dry deserts? Choose from oil, salt or water.
Water is scarce in dry deserts. Living things there are adapted to this.
What surrounds an island in the sea? Choose from mountain, sea or forest.
A sea island has seawater on every side.
What belongs in a forest? Choose from tree, fish or glass.
Trees are an important part of a forest.
What can be folded up and show your walking route? Choose from globe, compass or map.
A paper map folds up and can be used on a walk.
Which model shows Earth's other side when you turn it? Choose from compass, globe or map.
Turning a globe lets you see other parts of Earth.
What can hide the sun in the sky? Choose from cloud, bone or iron.
Clouds can partly or completely block sunlight.
What can help melt snow in spring? Choose from moon, paper or sun.
Snow can melt when the sun warms the ground.
What is long, flows and has two banks? Choose from island, river or sea.
A river flows between its two banks.
Which landscape has a high peak? Choose from mountain, forest or sea.
A mountain has a summit. Not every summit is pointed.
Which large body of water is normally salty? Choose from river, paper or sea.
Seawater contains dissolved salts. Do not drink it.
Which instrument uses a magnetic needle to show north for your map? Choose from globe, compass or map.
A compass helps you align the map's north direction.
Which kind of precipitation is liquid? Choose from rain, snow or cloud.
Rain falls as liquid drops. Snow falls as solid ice crystals.
Which is a star: the sun, a cloud or the moon? Choose from cloud, moon or sun.
The sun is a star and gives off its own light.
Which celestial body supplies most of the light reflected by the Moon? Choose from cloud, sun or moon.
The moon does not make its own light. It reflects sunlight.
What do rain and rivers bring to many plants? Choose from water, oil or salt.
Rain and rivers can supply plants with water.
